title: Immunodetection of α-synuclein Pathology in Murine Liver Tissues
author: Hallbeck, Ntzouni, et al.

steps.title: Prepare CO₂ euthanasia chamber
steps.instruction: Connect compressed CO₂ to the mouse euthanasia chamber, block the exit with a rubber stop, and ensure the chamber is clear for visual monitoring throughout the procedure.

steps.title: Euthanize mouse with CO₂
steps.instruction: Place the mouse in the chamber and introduce CO₂ gradually, increasing concentration from 30 % to 70 % over 2–3 min; maintain exposure for an additional 60 s after visual confirmation of respiratory cessation, then clean the chamber before the next use.

steps.title: Confirm death and secure mouse
steps.instruction: Verify death by checking for fixed, dilated pupils, then fix the paws to the bench with laboratory tape to secure the mouse for dissection.

steps.title: Expose thoracic cavity
steps.instruction: Lift the skin at the mid‑belly, make an incision extending to the chest cavity, cut the diaphragm immediately after exposing internal organs, and use thick scissors to cut the rib cage for easier heart access.

steps.title: Prepare perfusion syringe
steps.instruction: Load a butterfly needle attached to a 50 mL syringe with cold (4 °C) 1× PBS (pH 7.4).

steps.title: Perfuse mouse circulatory system
steps.instruction: Insert the needle halfway through the left ventricle, make a small incision in the right atrium, and gently inject at least 30 mL of cold PBS until the liver turns light pink, indicating complete blood removal.

substeps.instruction: If downstream applications (e.g., Western blot, ELISA) require cross‑linking, follow the PBS perfusion with at least 30 mL of cold (4 °C) 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) to improve fixation.

steps.title: Isolate liver
steps.instruction: Move the intestines aside with a small spatula, then use blunt forceps and small scissors to cut the portal vein and vena cava, detaching the liver without damaging the lobes.

steps.title: Fix liver in PFA
steps.instruction: Immerse the whole liver (or required portion) in cold (4 °C) 4 % PFA at 20 mL per liver in a 50 mL Falcon tube, keep the tube on wet ice, and incubate for 48 h; never keep the liver at room temperature (≈23 °C) as this reduces fixation effectiveness.

steps.title: Permeabilize tissue sections
steps.instruction: Incubate slides in Triton Permeabilization Solution for 45 min at room temperature (23 °C) with gentle shaking on a bench‑top shaker.

steps.title: Rinse after permeabilization
steps.instruction: Rinse slides with 1× PBS (pH 7.4) for 5 min, repeat twice for a total of 15 min to remove excess Triton‑X‑100.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Incubate slides in Tissue Blocking Solution for 1 h at room temperature (23 °C) with gentle shaking.

steps.title: Dry slides gently
steps.instruction: Quickly dry the area around the tissue with a napkin, taking care not to scratch the section.

steps.title: Create hydrophobic barrier
steps.instruction: Draw a hydrophobic barrier around the tissue using a hydrophobic pen while ensuring the tissue does not dry out; this reduces antibody volume needed.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Apply primary antibody diluted in Antibody Dilution Buffer to the tissue area and incubate overnight (18–24 h) at 4 °C; include control sections lacking primary and secondary antibodies to assess background.

substeps.instruction: If two primary antibodies from different species are required, add both simultaneously, ensuring non‑overlapping epitopes.
Titrate each antibody batch as needed because concentration variations can affect staining.

steps.title: PBS rinse post‑primary
steps.instruction: Incubate the entire slide in 1× PBS (pH 7.4) for 5 min with gentle shaking, repeat twice for a total of 15 min.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the tissue (within the hydrophobic barrier) with secondary antibody in Antibody Dilution Buffer for 2 h at room temperature (23 °C); cover the slide with foil to prevent photobleaching.

steps.title: PBS rinse post‑secondary
steps.instruction: Incubate the entire slide in 1× PBS for 5 min with gentle shaking, repeat twice for a total of 15 min.

steps.title: Optional nuclear staining
steps.instruction: If nuclear staining is desired, incubate the tissue area with Hoechst solution for 10 min, then rinse the whole slide with 1× PBS for an additional 10 min.

steps.title: Lipofuscin blocking
steps.instruction: Incubate slides in lipofuscin blocking solution for 1–3 min, then quickly dip (≈1 sec) in 70 % ethanol to remove unbound material.

steps.title: Final PBS rinse
steps.instruction: Rinse slides in 1× PBS (pH 7.4) for 10 min.

steps.title: Mount with Vectashield
steps.instruction: Add 1–2 drops of Vectashield fluorescence mounting medium (depending on tissue size) onto the slide and place a coverslip immediately.

steps.title: Remove excess mounting medium
steps.instruction: Gently press the coverslip with a dry paper towel to eliminate excess medium and any bubbles.

steps.title: Seal and dry slides
steps.instruction: Seal the coverslip and slide edges with standard nail‑polish solution, allow to dry for 30–60 min while protecting from light to prevent photobleaching.

description: In Parkinson’s disease (PD), alpha-Synuclein (α-Syn) pathology is not limited to the brain, as it has also been identified in multiple organs within the peripheral nervous system (PNS),1 and reviewed extensively.2,3 Thus, detection of α-Syn pathology in peripheral tissues may represent an early feature of PD pathogenesis1,4,5,6 and could potentially serve as a biomarker for disease diagnosis and progression.2,3 However, protocols for the immunodetection of α-Syn in peripheral tissues, whether from PD cases or in animal models of the disease, require reliable techniques to provide consistent results. The protocol herein offers a comprehensive method for the immunodetection of total and modified α-Syn pathology in paraffin-embedded murine liver tissue sections. We recently adopted this protocol for the immunodetection of total and modified α-Syn by tyrosine nitration (nY39), phosphorylation (pY39, pS87 and pS129, Y133) and C-terminal truncation events (X-122) in mouse models of PD (A30P, L61)7,8 and multiple system atrophy (MSA29).9 This protocol adds solutions to troubleshooting steps for tissue isolation, fixation and embedding, immunostaining and image analysis, helping to validate the presence of human α-Syn pathology in the liver, where we hypothesize its involvement in the clearance of PD associated pathology.
